chunks: To call on Him is true (supplication). For those they invoke other than Him do not answer them at all, except like a man who stretches his hands towards the water that it reach his mouth, but it will never reach it. Not more than error are the prayers of infidels.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used in the Quran to describe the futility of calling upon false gods?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the ontological superiority of Allah’s response compared to the absolute impotence of idols, which cannot even grant a trivial need like water. The metaphor of the thirsty man stretching his hands illustrates the futility of polytheistic supplication, emphasizing that while idols are physically present, they are spiritually void and unable to intercede or answer. This reinforces the concept of Tawhid al-Ibadah, where worship is directed solely to the One who truly hears and responds.
